text: Knocklyon (Irish: Cnoc Lín) is a suburb of Dublin located in South Dublin, Ireland, situated in the southwest of the city in the foothills of the Dublin Mountains and immediately south of the River Dodder. Unlike many Dublin suburbs, it was not developed around a traditional village and is primarily composed of modern housing, with a few old cottages and farmhouses along Knocklyon Road reflecting its rural origins. Historically, the area was known in 14th-century scrolls as Cnoclín, meaning 'flax mountain'. Until recently, roadsigns incorrectly used a "reverse anglicised" translation, displaying "Lyon's hill" or "Bóthar Chnoc Liamhna", which has since been corrected by the local authority following recommendations from the Irish Placenames Commission. The suburb is bordered to the west by Firhouse and Ballycullen, to the east and south by Rathfarnham and Ballyboden, and to the north, across the River Dodder, by Templeogue. The construction of the M50 motorway divided Knocklyon, with most of the area now lying east of the motorway; housing estates to the east include Idrone, Green Acre Court, Knocklyon Avenue, Beverly, Dargle Wood, Coolamber, Knockcullen, Lansdowne, Delaford, Knockaire (in the old Knocklyon townland), and Orlagh, Scholarstown Park, and Templeoran (in Scholarstown townland), while to the west are Castlefield, Glenlyon, Dalriada, Glenvara, and Woodstown. The western and eastern parts are connected via Firhouse Road, the M50 flyover at Junction 12, and a footbridge near where the Old Knocklyon Road met Ballycullen Road. The population cannot be isolated due to the area being part of the Firhouse-Knocklyon electoral division (39,602 in 2011), plus portions of Ballyboden ED (57,085) and Firhouse-Ballycullen ED (77,773), which are not separately published. Knocklyon Shopping Centre features a supermarket and other retail outlets, with two smaller shopping sites in Orlagh and Woodstown, each anchored by a convenience store and including takeaway food shops, beauty salons, and other services, plus a local public house. A St. John Ambulance first aid training division was established in 2010, and the Rutland Centre, a private addiction rehabilitation facility, is located on Knocklyon Road. The area includes several open spaces, such as those along the River Dodder and within residential estates, hosting playing pitches for Ballyboden St. Enda's GAA and Knocklyon United Football Club. Community facilities include the Iona Centre and the Knocklyon Community Centre, which supports sports and social groups. St. Colmcille's National School opened in September 1976, is the largest primary school in Ireland and one of the largest in Europe, educating 1,600 students with 80 teachers, 23 special needs assistants, and 11 ancillary staff, and Gaelscoil Chnoc Liamhna, an Irish language primary school established in September 1996 with 36 pupils, now teaching over 200 children. St. Colmcille's Community School (formerly Knocklyon Community School), opened in September 2000, serves around 700 secondary students. The Catholic Parish of Knocklyon was established in October 1974 under the patronage of Saint Colmcille, part of the Dublin Archdiocese, previously administered by the Carmelite Order until 2022 and now under the Divine Word Missionaries since 2023; its parish church opened in April 1980. The Iona Pastoral Centre, opened in 2000, hosts prayer groups, social activities (such as pilates, mother and baby groups, knitting, and bridge), and includes a St Vincent de Paul chapter, AA meetings, and GROW Mental Health Movement. The parish publishes the Knocklyon News magazine since 1982, three to four times per year with a print run of 5,000, featuring community and faith-based content. Church of Ireland residents attend Rathfarnham Parish Church, and the Knocklyon Church of Christ is an autonomous Christian congregation with premises on Knocklyon Road near Gaelscoil Chnoc Liamhna. Dublin Bus routes serving the area include 15, F1, S6, and S8. The GAA is represented by Ballyboden St. Enda's GAA Club, and association football is managed by Knocklyon United F.C.; the Brothers Pearse Athletics Club was founded in 1956. The district also hosts the Knocklyon Junior Badminton Club and Knocklyon Social Badminton, both operating from the Knocklyon Community Centre. A Scouting Ireland branch and the South Dublin Model Railway Club operate from their own premises, and the Knocklyon Concert Band, a brass band operating for over 20 years, is active in the community. Local businesses and community groups are supported by Knocklyon Network, an active networking organisation.
